questions.question: Some OP-01 decisions are just an option letter, e.g. D3 Decision = "(a).". What should the Observed column hold in that case?

options.label: Expand to option text (Recommended)
options.description: Replace a leading "(a)" with that option's text from the Options field, keeping any elaboration after it. D3 becomes "(a) encoding default UTF-8 and errors default strict, both fixed by the library, never the locale".

options.label: Verbatim only
options.description: Keep the Decision field exactly as written. D3 stays "(a).", which is accurate but tells the reader nothing.

options.label: Fall back to Recommendation
options.description: When the decision is a bare letter matching the recommended one, show the Recommendation text instead.

questions.question: You said "scenarios and recommendations". Should the Recommendation field become its own column?

options.label: No, 3 columns
options.description: Heading | Scenario | Observed, as in the sample.

options.label: Yes, 4 columns
options.description: Heading | Scenario | Recommendation | Observed. Shows where the decision departed from the recommendation, as in D2.

options.label: All decided entries

options.label: Decision = recommendation
options.description: Only decisions that took the recommended option. Drops entries like D2, where the maintainer chose (c) over the recommended (a).

Which OP-01 cluster should the spike's first vertical slice (typed rows → Python reference model → checks) cover?

options.label: Stream lifecycle (Recommended)
options.description: D6, D7, D15 to D18, D20, D36. A state machine with data; no backend or concurrency needed; shows how rows become transitions.

options.label: Key classification
options.description: D4, D8, D9, D34. Smallest slice: a total partition plus an error-category table. Quick to finish, but it only exercises a pure function, not the protocol.

options.label: Pinning under writes
options.description: D21, D22, D25, D26. Closest to the TLA+ layer and the highest value, but it needs a concurrency model, so it is a larger first step.

questions.question: May the slice read the OP-01 record again to cite exact clauses, or should it stay strictly with what is already in context?

options.label: Context only (Recommended)
options.description: Everything the stream slice needs is already in context. Keeps the 'no further repo reads' rule.

options.label: Allow record reads
options.description: Re-read OP-01.md as needed, e.g. for D41's register or the O-items. Needed if the classification or pinning slice is chosen.

Where should the OP-01 stream spike land? BK-506 reserves sdd/research/bk-506-faithfulness-trial/ for its pre-registered trial, and RFC-0029 R4 keeps record-derived oracle work away from it.

options.label: bk-485-op01-stream-spike/ (Recommended)
options.description: sdd/research/bk-485-op01-stream-spike/ with README + repo-only report.md, under BK-485 (step 5's model and 0.33 comparison). The report states that it is not BK-506's trial and must not feed it.

options.label: Under BK-505 instead
options.description: File it as record-quality evidence (one extraction of OP-01, stale-filter finding). Fits the extraction half; the conformance half fits BK-505 less well.

questions.question: Rule RF4 assumes a cancellation is ignored when a read needs no transfer, which O45 reads as contradicting D20 ('a cancelled stream read ... is then Closed', in every state). Fix it before landing?

options.label: Fix RF4, rerun, then land (Recommended)
options.description: Make cancellation close the stream in every state per D20, rerun all four SUTs, and record the before/after. The committed oracle then matches the record as the audit reads it.

options.label: Land as run, note it
options.description: Freeze the spike exactly as it ran, and record RF4's conflict with D20 as a known defect in the report.

questions.question: What should ship alongside the spike folder?

options.label: Trace + BK-485 dossier line (Recommended)
options.description: sdd/traces/bk-485-op01-stream-spike.yml (precedent: bk-484-key-model-research.yml), plus one line in BK-485's dossier pointing to the spike. No backlog items, no CHANGELOG (contributor-process only).

options.label: Trace only
options.description: Ship the trace and leave BK-485's dossier and body untouched; the spike is discoverable only through sdd/research/ and the trace.

options.label: Folder only
options.description: No trace and no dossier line. Lightest, but breaks the precedent that research on a backlog item ships its trace.

questions.question: The first spike step (extract_decisions.py, the 24-row table) used each decision's own 'Open items' field, which later reopens (O14 to O45) never update. Include it?

options.label: Include with caveat (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the script and its output as step 1, with the report stating the filter is stale and that the Axis status table is the current source. That is itself a BK-505 data point.

options.label: Drop it
options.description: Land only the stream slice (rules, model, conformance). The stale-filter observation survives as one line in the report.
